scope: Where an ERISC's cycles go, split by source line (addr2line inline chains). Descriptive only: a profile does not say which ERISC bounds a row or why one router is faster (repo CLAUDE.md).

categories.label: Packet polls and room checks
categories.def: Per-pass tests for work. Is there a packet: the receive ring's packets-received register, a sender channel's free-slots register. Is there room: free slots in the far receiver's ring, downstream admission, a transaction ID free for reuse.
categories.notes: Idle time shares these lines with real work, and it cannot be separated by profile: a router polls without stopping, so an empty pass runs the same tests as a busy one and skips the work. The receiver's early return on a pass with no packet ready is counted here. A register read stalls at its first use: on main the load and its test are separate lines, both counted here. On a forwarding router the downstream credit reads count here.

categories.label: Header and route decode
categories.def: Locating and reading the packet header, decoding the route (forward, deliver or both, and which downstreams), dispatching on the command type, and rewriting the header for the next hop.
categories.notes: The header word's load latency shows where it is first used. That is usually here (the route test or the command switch), but it can land in a NoC command when the command reads the header first.

categories.label: NoC commands
categories.def: Forwarding to a downstream router and delivering locally (write, scatter, atomic, inline write): command-buffer waits, register writes, transaction IDs, and the downstream ring's slot and credit-register updates that go with a forward.
categories.notes: Command-buffer ready spins are counted here because they are part of issuing a command, not idle passes.

categories.label: Ethernet send
categories.def: Sending a packet over the link: the header size read, TX-queue status checks and busy spins, the TX-queue register writes, the far ring's packets-received update, and advancing the channel's and the far ring's slots.
categories.notes: Credit-counter loads that the new router places inside the send are counted under credits. Their latency can show at a send line that follows them.

categories.label: Acks, completions and credits
categories.def: Receiving ERISC: first-level acks, completion proofs (have the slot's NoC writes left), credit messages and frames to the far sender, and releasing a slot after dispatch (ring counters, source-channel record). Sending ERISC: reading and processing the far receiver's acks and completions, and crediting producers (worker semaphore writes, upstream router credit registers).
categories.notes: Per-pass credit tests (are there new completions or acks?) count here, with their idle time. Releasing a slot is counted here because it is what makes the slot creditable. The receiver's partial-group timeout count, which runs only on passes with no packet, is counted here with the credit decision it belongs to.

categories.label: Connection and loop overhead
categories.def: Worker connection and teardown checks, termination and context-switch checks, round and loop bookkeeping, the pass structure (channel visits, out-of-line pass calls, saving and reloading per-channel state), telemetry and trimming hooks.
categories.notes: Outer-loop fallback rules map here. Lines that reach this category only through a fallback rule are listed for review in each validation report.

categories.label: Other router code
categories.def: Router code outside the steady-state loop (init, rare paths) that a rule names explicitly.
categories.notes: Unmapped samples (no rule anywhere in the chain) are reported separately and are not part of this category.

excluded: Samples outside the kernel image (firmware, the idle context switch) and the first and last 5% of each target's kernel samples (outside the traffic window). Shares are of the kernel samples in the window.
noise: About 500 samples per run is roughly +/-2.5 cycles per entry. Entries under 3 cycles/packet are flagged as noise. Every record carries its sample count.

dropped.why: Lines that run only on empty passes came to 0.0-0.1 cycles/packet on every sample set: idle time lands in the per-pass lines (checks, credits, loop), not in idle-only code, so a 'waiting' bar would mislead.
dropped.instead: Spare time per ERISC from the one-side delay A/Bs (slack.json), attached to the new router's records as spare_cycles / spare_label; main has no such measurement (spare_cycles null, said so in spare_label).
